item.title: Candace Owens fires back at Laura Loomer over George Farmer claim as viral arrest record claim sparks intense online backlash
item.description: Candace Owens denied Laura Loomer’s viral claim that an arrest record belonged to her husband George Farmer. Owens said key details were missing and called the post misleading. The issue spread quickly online, dividing opinions. While some supported Owens, others asked for verification. No confirmed evidence has linked the record to Farmer so far.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: IShowSpeed blushes after ex Vanessa’s flirty birthday donation goes viral
item.description: Internet sensation IShowSpeed was left blushing during his 21st birthday stream when his ex-girlfriend, Vanessa Anne Williams, sent a flirty donation. The message, hinting at reconciliation and referencing her Miami location, reignited fan speculation about their past relationship and potential reunion. The streamer's shy reaction quickly became a viral moment, leaving fans eager for updates.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Is Paula Badosa retiring at 28? Injury struggles and ranking fall outside top 100 raise concern after emotional message
item.description: Paula Badosa is facing one of the toughest phases of her career with injury, ranking drop, and mental struggles. After falling outside the top 100, she shared emotional thoughts about fear and self-doubt. Despite her split with Stefanos Tsitsipas and ongoing pain, she says she will keep fighting and believes she can return stronger again.

item.title: Is there a second Sphinx under Giza? New scans spark shocking underground megastructure claims
item.description: Advanced radar scans at Giza Plateau suggest a vast underground network of structures, potentially including a "second Sphinx." Researchers from the Khafre Research Project detected organized formations, deep chambers, and interconnected pathways beneath the sands. These findings, while debated by some experts, revive ancient theories of hidden chambers and reignite fascination with the site's unexplored depths.

item.title: Tectone YouTube ban leads to Rumble switch, streamer quits Twitch and YouTube
item.description: Tectone has announced a significant move, leaving both YouTube and Twitch to become an exclusive streamer on Rumble. This decision follows a recent one-week ban from YouTube for "excessive swearing," prompting him to seek a platform with more perceived freedom. His first Rumble stream is scheduled for March 28, though censored videos will still appear on YouTube.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: YouTuber Matt Walsh calls out viral teen ignorance video and pushes for voting age change to 25
item.description: A viral spring break video showed US teens struggling with basic current affairs questions. Matt Walsh reacted strongly, saying young people lack awareness and should not vote at 18. He called for raising the voting age to 25 and also criticized the US education system, linking it to poor knowledge and growing dependence on AI tools like ChatGPT.

item.title: What is ‘launching soon’? White House official page posts strange, unexplained videos amid US‑Iran war
item.description: Amid escalating US‑Iran tensions, the White House posted two cryptic videos, one deleted within 90 minutes, that quickly fueled online speculation. Lacking context or narrative, the clips prompted theories ranging from apps and space missions to military strikes, with many users conjuring ominous conspiracies. Despite millions of views, the White House offered no clarification, leaving the posts mysterious and widely debated.

10 abandoned islands in the world no one dares to live on and the chilling reasons why
item.description: Throughout the world, some islands were once inhabited by humans but now remain uninhabited due to various reasons such as environmental, conflict, or economic factors. Although these islands may appear to be mysterious, studies indicate that abandonment is not a rare occurrence. Recently, a study on island biogeography established that about 30% of islands have been abandoned within the last 150 years, especially those that are smaller and more isolated.The study established that abandonment is a common occurrence on islands due to limited resources and harsh environments. Today, these islands are being used for scientific study and protected by various governments for their historical and environmental importance. From industrial sites to hostile environments, each island has a different story to tell. Natural disasters, rising sea levels, and the introduction of invasive species can also make islands difficult to inhabit. Over time, these pressures lead communities to relocate, leaving behind structures that slowly decay.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Jarvis Butts found dead two weeks after sentencing for the murder of 13-year-old girl Na’Ziyah Harris
item.description: Jarvis Butts, convicted of murdering 13-year-old Na’Ziyah Harris and multiple sexual offenses, has died in custody two weeks after his sentencing. Authorities are investigating his death as a possible suicide. Butts had pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and criminal sexual conduct, receiving a significant prison sentence. The case remains unresolved as Na’Ziyah Harris's body has not been recovered.

item.title: Who is Ben Azelart? Sidemen Inside feature sparks buzz over his $1.2 million YouTube video claim
item.description: Ben Azelart is trending after claiming he earned $1.2 million from a single YouTube video on Sidemen Inside Season 3. The clip, shared by Jack Manifold on X, quickly went viral. Despite this, Azelart says his success came from steady growth, not one viral moment, as he built his career from skateboarding videos to global content creation.

item.title: 'Keep ‌blowing them away': Trump renews warning as he claims Iran 'begging' for deal
item.description: President Trump stated Iran is "begging" for a deal to end the war and warned of further strikes if nuclear ambitions are not abandoned. He indicated diplomacy might be closing, while US military operations are ahead of schedule. The conflict has resulted in over 3,000 deaths and millions displaced.

item.title: US, UK, EU push back on UN slavery reparations, despite acknowledging historical injustice
item.description: The UN General Assembly recognized the transatlantic slave trade as “the gravest crime against humanity,” aiming to confront historical injustice and advance reparatory justice. The resolution passed with 123 votes in favor. The US, Israel, and Argentina voted against it, while the UK and EU member states abstained over legal and reparations concerns, despite acknowledging slavery’s history. Ghana emphasized accountability, reparations, and long-term consequences for victims and their descendants.
